solution groups one-repo projects: h9k solution add, show, list, link, unlink, rename and close, with membership travelling as a team setting on every member, exactly one solution per project, and a cross-project board.\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022h9k solution add --title \\u003Ct\\u003E --project \\u003Cp\\u003E (repeatable) creates a node-scoped Solution record (a SolutionAggregate with SolutionAdded carrying id, key and title, plus SolutionRenamed and SolutionClosed with a reason, event-sourced like Epic) and writes a SolutionMembership (solution key, title, and every member by project key with its name and repository URL) into each named project\\u0027s team settings in that one command.\u0022,\u0022The membership travels through the existing ProjectTeamSettingsChanged path with no new replication path; a node receiving a membership for a solution it has never seen mirrors a local Solution record from it, the way ProjectKeyAssigned mirrors a ledger fact locally.\u0022,\u0022A project belongs to exactly one solution, enforced in the decider: h9k solution link refuses a project already in a solution and names that solution, h9k solution unlink is the explicit act that frees it first, and the setting is a single value in storage.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution link (and add) warns and asks for confirmation when the new member\\u0027s repository owner or organization differs from every existing member\\u0027s; a flag answers that confirmation for non-interactive use.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution rename and h9k solution close --reason are explicit human acts; nothing closes a solution automatically, including every member being archived.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution show \\u003Cs\\u003E composes the solution\\u0027s board across members grouped by project, every row a task id plus a plain description, and lists members this node has not joined by name and repository URL.\u0022,\u0022h9k solution list exists, h9k project show gains a Solution row, and task list and epic list accept --solution, resolved to the member projects known on this node.\u0022,\u0022Every new command and option carries help that teaches the ladder solution, project, epic, task, and every refusal quotes the rule it enforces.\u0022,\u0022Unit tests cover the aggregate, the membership round trip through the team-settings event, the one-solution refusal, the owner-mismatch warning decision, and board composition; no test creates a branch or touches GitHub.\u0022,\u0022docs/scope.md, docs/concepts.md and the hall9k-cli-reference skill describe the solution concept and its commands.\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Multi-repo projects: one hall9k project whose work spans several GitHub repositories (for example a backend API and infrastructure repo, a frontend repo, and a couple of others). Today a project has exactly one repo; a new project of Brian\\u0027s needs several.\\n\\nDiscovery for idea f8212260 is in the idea\\u0027s workspace: findings.md (the design, the name, the hard-to-reverse choices) and journal.md (Brian\\u0027s rulings on 2026-10-29). Model the membership on ContextLinks: a named record, replace-the-whole-list semantics on ProjectTeamSettingsChanged, a repeatable flag. Members are named by project key (the 26-character ULID from the ledger genesis, identical across nodes), never by local project id. The one-solution rule exists for a security reason Brian gave: a project in two solutions would put each solution\\u0027s member names and repository URLs in front of the other solution\\u0027s teammates. This piece changes nothing in dispatch, delivery, review, closeout or the gh layer. It is the base of a stack: solution epics stack on it, the solution window and onboarding are blocked by it.\\n\\nDiscovery workspace (research notes, gathered files, and prototypes from before this was a task; may be empty):\\n/Users/brianhallmanac/.hall9k/projects/hall9k/ideas/f8212260-multi-repo-projects-one-hall9k-project-whose-work-spans-seve/workspace\u0022,\u0022Constraints\u0022:null,\u0022ExternalReference\u0022:null,\u0022AddedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-29T15:02:42.602901\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022AddedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022Model\u0022:\u0022\u0022,\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:[],\u0022StartsAsDraft\u0022:true,\u0022SourceIdeaId\u0022:\u002201a187ae-89fb-73e3-9a59-f48af8212260\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:\u002201a1882e-f056-7728-961d-e29361a43d0a\u0022,\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:null,\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:null,\u0022PreApproved\u0022:false,\u0022Origin\u0022:null,\u0022PreApproval\u0022:\u0022Off\u0022,\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:null,\u0022SecondaryExternalReference\u0022:null,\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:null,\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:null,\u0022InitialScope\u0022:\u0022Fleet\u0022}","originEventId":"ba19618c-26e9-4fa4-aa52-94990908d9fd","originSequence":139793,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-29T15:02:42.616446+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"}]
